claims.statement: SQL lifecycle wrappers delegate to shared create, alter and drop implementations; caller-controlled names and query preparation use captured caller context, and create checks output-schema/source access while alter requires ownership.

Creation orders query admission and cycle checks before guarded storage creation, persists metadata and dependency edges before capture setup, then transfers ownership, initializes when allowed and invalidates the derived DAG.

Catalog persistence connects stream identity and storage to per-source dependency edges containing column usage and table-like source snapshots/fingerprints; rewritten view sources can additionally have soft dependencies for DDL tracking.
AUTO is an admission request that begins as DIFFERENTIAL and may fall back to FULL, not a persisted RefreshMode execution variant; requested and effective refresh modes are recorded separately.

Refresh mode, population/frontier/reinitialization state, operational status and orchestration ownership are distinct axes; manual refresh can choose full work for a differential stream without a frontier and reinitialization for needs_reinit.
EXTERNAL creation suppresses initialization and rejects IMMEDIATE; ordinary manual refresh and refresh-affecting alterations reject EXTERNAL streams in favor of coordinator or MANAGED ownership.

Base-table CDC is source-shared: the first consumer creates capture infrastructure and later consumers join tracking, widen referenced capture columns when needed and invalidate affected MERGE caches.

Scheduled source setup distinguishes base-table CDC, foreign-table and materialized-view polling, and upstream stream-table change buffers; IMMEDIATE uses IVM triggers, while mixed immediate/deferred source consumers still require CDC.
Diamond consistency defaults to atomic with fastest scheduling; slowest requires atomic, and detected convergence with consistency disabled emits an inconsistency notice.

Circular dependency admission is opt-in and requires DIFFERENTIAL members with verifiable monotone queries; ALTER replaces incoming edges and validates the proposed query, with SCC identities persisted for cyclic members.

Execution-unit graph construction handles cyclic SCCs and consistency groups and conservatively folds downstream IMMEDIATE closures into execution units rather than treating every stream as independently scheduled.

Manual refresh rejects recovery replicas, CDC hold, suspended/error and external targets; advisory and catalog row locking coordinate concurrent work, followed by metadata reload to avoid stale-frontier replay.
Manual refresh separates privileged bookkeeping and internal DML-guard bypass from definition-derived SQL executed in stream-owner context.

If-not-exists preserves an existing definition, while create-or-replace compares rewritten whitespace-normalized SQL and configuration, no-ops when identical and delegates changes to ALTER rather than unconditional drop/create.

Query ALTER validates and classifies proposed state reuse under target and source locks; non-compatible admitted changes suspend the stream, build isolated shadow storage, reset frontier/population, reconcile dependencies and capture, fully populate then atomically swap and reactivate.

Semantic query replacement does not reuse the old frontier just because the output schema matches; retained capture may require wider columns or IVM retargeting, and publication bindings can block storage replacement.

Durable query-alter changes rely on surrounding transaction rollback to restore old auxiliary state, while cache prewarming and some resource cleanups are best-effort rather than unconditional transactional guarantees.

Source DDL hooks fail closed when dependency relevance cannot be inspected and classify changes using saved state; column-affecting DDL is blocked by default by block_source_ddl and other changes may invalidate contracts or suspend streams.

Drop pre-authorizes the downstream plan, rejects dependents without cascade and prevalidates publications before mutation; per-stream removal locks lifecycle state, removes storage/auxiliary state/catalog dependencies, and invalidates derived graphs and templates.

Capture teardown is last-consumer based on surviving dependency edges, excluding the altered stream when needed; it releases base CDC resources and legacy WAL artifacts only when unreferenced and removes unused stream change buffers without dropping base sources.

Focused lifecycle tests cover identical replacement preserving timestamp/count, semantic same-schema replacement changing OID, invalid-query and cycle rejection preserving the original active populated stream, shared CDC retention, and fail-closed DDL guards.
